newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy March new car sales seen up 25-28 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy March new car sales seen up 25-28 pct.

text.p: Italian new car registrations in March are likely to post a rise of some 25 to 28 percent year-on-year to 220,000-225,000 units as the domestic market continues to recover, auto sector analysts and sources said.
Registrations in March 1996 totalled 176,333. In February this year registrations jumped 21.45 percent to 198,000, boosted by the government's car buying incentive scheme introduced in January.

"An increase of around 25 percent is very likely in March and also in the following months," said Giuliana Porta of brokers Albertini Sim. "Orders have grown by 30-35 percent on average but deliveries have not increased at the same pace. I think the full effect of this will be seen in March," she said.

"Research by (auto sector body) Centro Studi Promotor shows that in February, 87 percent of dealers saw orders at a high level against 65 percent in January. So it's likely March will see an increase above that in February," said JP Morgan analyst Ilaria Fornari.

One analyst who declined to be named said March sales could be above 25 percent. "The rise in orders has meant longer delivery times so the cumulative effect could result in a rise in registrations of around 27 to 28 percent," he said.
The transport ministry is due to publish official March new registration figures on Thursday, April 10.
CSP forecasts total 1997 new car registrations at above two million units against 1.74 million in 1996, CSP director Gian Primo Quagliano told Reuters.

But to stay around the two million figure in 1998 "we will need a recovering economy and an extension of the incentive scheme (due to end in September). Without these two conditions new registrations could return to a level below 1.7 million," he said.
